newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall, seen in horizontal trend.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall, seen in horizontal trend.

text.p: Polish shares fell in lower turnover on Tuesday and analysts saw them maintaining their three-week horizontal trend amid a lack of fresh signals to spur significant gains or losses.
The main market's WIG index fell 0.6 percent, to 13,659.9, and turnover fell 11.8 percent to 70.4 million zlotys ($25.1 million) on both markets as 40 issues fell, 25 rose and 18 were flat.

"There are no reasons for futher falls as the main index has already significantly fallen from a high around 15,000, nor for rises, so the market is flat in low turnovers," said Jan Koch, a trader at Polish Development Bank (PBR) brokerage.
Some analysts said there was a chance a downtrend could emerge near year-end, which often sees profit-taking, and because 1996 earnings have proved disappointing for many firms.
He said that less than half of listed companies showed profit growth in real terms in the first 10 months of the year.
Continuous trade turnover was at 2.1 million zlotys ($0.8 million) with three stocks down, one up and four flat.
Mass privatisation NFI units rose 1.7 percent in 36.6-million-zloty ($13.1 million) continuous trade but fell 5.2 percent in a 27-million-zloty ($9.6 million) turnover in the regular session.

Analysts said Bank Slaski, which on Tuesday was given by the IBCA rating agency a BBB rating for long-term debt, an A3 rating for short-term debt and an individual rating of C, could experience a brief rise.
